sources.heading: Where does this information come from?
sources.footnote: Barrierefri is a private project, not a public authority. The municipality or transport operator decides when a barrier is fixed.

reports.title: The report and photo
reports.text: Written by the person who reported the barrier. Barrierefri doesn't check reports before they're shown, but staff can reject them with a reason.

deadline.title: Deadline for fixing it
deadline.text: The deadlines don't come from a law or a public authority. Barrierefri set them based on how much the barrier blocks: 2 days for a lift, 3 for a blocked pavement, 7 for an audio signal, 30 for anything else, 60 for an entrance and 90 for kerbs and ramps.

confirmations.title: Confirmations
confirmations.text: People who have been past answer whether the barrier is still there. Barrierefri turns the answers into an estimate. A new report starts at two thirds, so no single answer can settle it.

map.title: The map
map.text: Map data from OpenStreetMap and its contributors.
